original_question: Let R be a commutative base ring, let A be an R-algebra, and let delta be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation. Here an R-derivation is an R-linear map D: A -> A satisfying D(ab) = D(a)b + aD(b), and an R-E-derivation is an R-linear map delta: A -> A satisfying delta(ab) = delta(a)b + adelta(b) - delta(a)delta(b), equivalently delta = I - phi for some R-algebra endomorphism phi. For every left, right, or two-sided ideal I of A, what is the radical r(delta(I)), where r(V) denotes the set of all a in A such that a^m belongs to V for all sufficiently large m?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 1.4(A) (the LFNED Problem): "Find the radical of δ(I) for all one-sided or two sided ideals I of A."
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact introductory problem. It has the right ambient data (a commutative base ring R, an R-algebra A, and δ either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation), the right class of ideals (left, right, or two-sided), and the right radical notion r(V) defined by eventual membership of powers. It also correctly records the equivalent description of an R-E-derivation as δ = I - φ for an R-algebra endomorphism φ.
missing_details: The exact target in the paper is not one of the later conjectures, but specifically Problem 1.4(A) in the introduction.
The paper allows A to be noncommutative; this is why one-sided ideals are explicitly included.
Part A of the problem has no local finiteness, local nilpotence, algebraicity, or characteristic-zero hypothesis; those restrictions appear only in the later LFED/LNED conjectures.
The radical r(V) is defined for an arbitrary R-subspace V of A, not just for ideals.
To make the statement fully stand-alone, spell out "for all sufficiently large m" as: there exists an integer N = N(a) such that a^m lies in δ(I) for every m >= N.
For paper-faithfulness, it helps to note that this radical question is posed as the first part of a broader program relating images of derivations/E-derivations to Mathieu subspaces.
refined_question: Let R be a commutative ring, let A be an arbitrary R-algebra (not assumed commutative), and let δ:A→A be either an R-derivation or an R-E-derivation, i.e. an R-linear map satisfying δ(ab)=δ(a)b+aδ(b)-δ(a)δ(b), equivalently δ=I-φ for some R-algebra endomorphism φ of A. For each left ideal, right ideal, or two-sided ideal I of A, determine the radical r(δ(I)), where for any R-subspace V⊆A one defines r(V):={a∈A | there exists N such that a^m∈V for all m≥N}.
justification: The draft is not best matched to the LFED or LNED conjectures, because those ask whether certain images are Mathieu subspaces under additional hypotheses such as local finiteness, local nilpotence, and characteristic zero. By contrast, your draft asks directly for the radical of δ(I) for arbitrary derivations/E-derivations and arbitrary one-sided or two-sided ideals, which is exactly the content of Problem 1.4(A) in the introduction. Definition 1.2 supplies the precise radical notation, and Lemma 1.3 explains why this radical question is important for the Mathieu-subspace questions that follow. The later theorem on algebraic algebras clarifies that controlling such images is closely tied to the Mathieu-subspace structure, but the nearest official formulation to your draft remains Problem 1.4(A).
